newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply lower as LME slides.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply lower as LME slides.

text.p: An options-fueled twister sent LME spiralling downwards, dragging New York's COMEX more than five cents lower in heavy trading despite the dearth of fresh fundamental news, traders and analysts said.
All the gains from last Friday's rally were wiped out to leave the market back at square one with fundamentals taking a back seat to technical signals and options activity, traders said.
Friday's LME stock report may provide direction.
Heavy delta options trading on the LME accelerated the red metal's downward path, breaking through the key $1,970 per tonne LME three-months price.

"New York was the tail of the dog - it was all London led," said William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch. "The options activity is feeding on itself and, frankly, it's being exacerbated by locals on the LME - they are not doing anything to smoothe it out."

December COMEX settled 5.40 cents weaker at 89.00 cents per pound, traded 93.90 to 88.90 cents. Spot September went out 5,25 cents weaker at 89.90 cents. Volume was heavy at an estimated 17,000 lots compared to Wednesday's official 7,540 lots.
